grand_strategy.reading: Romania is a frontline state with a rear-area politics. Its grand strategy is borrowed security: bind the United States, NATO and the EU to the Black Sea by hosting their bases, buying their arms with their loans and keeping Ukraine and Moldova alive as buffers. The method has worked in hardware (Kogalniceanu, Deveselu, F-35s, SAFE) and fails at the margin Washington controls: the brigade left in October 2025 while Bucharest was offering a base for the Iran operation five months later. What is new in 2026 is that the weak point is internal. The annulled election of 2024 did not remove the sovereigntist vote, a third of Parliament, and the fiscal repair that the EU and the rating agencies demanded took the coalition apart; the country has had a caretaker cabinet since 5 May and a fourth nominee since 5 October, with every agency one step above junk. Neighbours show the same split between kinship and interest: Moldova is kin and a partner, Ukraine is a partner and a dispute over Romanian schools, Hungary is a co-member whose new government (Magyar, April 2026) has restarted the conversation, Serbia is a partner it presses on the Vlachs, Turkey the one NATO ally in the Black Sea with ships and a strategic partnership. China is held at arm's length by law (the 5G rules that exclude Huawei) and, since Dan's remarks on the 2025 strategy, with open caution; Israel is a partner whose war Romania abstained on in 2023 and 2024 and voted for the Palestinian seat in 2026. Read through Luttwak, the danger is that Romania's policy of making itself useful rests on stable government in Bucharest, which is the thing it lacks.

stances.note: The 2025-2030 National Defence Strategy puts Russia's hybrid war and its aggression against Ukraine first among the threats, Moscow's drones have crossed, hit (Galati, 29 May 2026) and been shot down over Romania, and the two have traded consul and diplomat expulsions since 29 May 2026 (Constanta consulate closed; St Petersburg consulate closed 25 Jun; embassy official expelled and ambassador recalled 27 Jul). It stays rival, not adversary: no Romanian source states an aim of Russia's defeat or regime change, and the ontology keeps adversary for mortal enemies (Ukraine's grade toward Russia). Cooling because the incidents are now physical and the diplomatic channel is thinning. Bond - grievance: the Soviet legacy in Bessarabia and Northern Bukovina and the Dec 2024 election interference.

relations_from.summary: At the Ankara summit (7-8 Jul 2026) Romania asked for the Black Sea to be named in the declaration and obtained, per Curs de Guvernare's list, a NATO defence-bank office on the eastern flank, rotating command of the Combined Task Force Black Sea from 2028 and an extension of the NATO fuel pipeline network into Romania; Dan also proposed moving the NATO Black Sea centre from Istanbul to Constanta (target 2028).

President Dan says strategic partnership between Romania and Turkey could be expanded

relations_from.summary: Romania backs Moldova's EU path and defence of its sovereignty against Russia (trilateral with Sandu and Zelensky in Chisinau, 27 Aug 2026) but does not pursue unification. Sandu said in January 2026 she would vote for it and on 8 Oct 2026 that it needs a majority that polls do not show (33% IMAS July 2026; 44% against 39% ATES March 2026); about 1.5 million Moldovans hold Romanian citizenship.

Sandu: unification only with the will of the majority

relations_from.summary: Bucharest wants Ukraine to keep Romanian-language education for its minority under the 1997 treaty and the March 2026 declaration; Draft Law 16119 on the education of national minorities (registered 1 Oct 2026, committee recommended urgent adoption on 6 Oct) was due before the Rada on 12 Oct, and Romanian associations in Chernivtsi, Transcarpathia and Odesa asked for a postponement and for the recall of Ambassador Micula. Education minister Daniel David had already asked Kyiv to respect mother-tongue schooling.

sources.title: Bill on educational rights of national minorities challenged by associations of Romanians in Ukraine

relations_from.summary: Bucharest holds that all Serbian citizens attached to Romanian language, culture and faith, whether they call themselves Romanians or Vlachs, belong to the Romanian minority; Belgrade recognises Vlachs as a separate minority (21,013 at the 2022 census, 0.3%).

sources.title: A Security Conundrum in European Kin-State Politics: The (Mis)Recognition of Vlachs and Romanian-Serbian Relations

relations_from.summary: After Peter Magyar's election win (12 Apr 2026) Bucharest seeks a reset: Dan spoke of a new chapter, PM Bolojan phoned Magyar on 16 Apr and invited him to Bucharest, stressing economic ties and energy interconnection, and the UDMR (Hungarian minority party, in the coalition until May) agreed with Magyar on 21 Apr to cooperate transparently.

sources.title: Romanian PM speaks by phone with Hungary's Peter Magyar, invites him to Bucharest

relations_from.summary: Strategic partnership declaration signed in Bucharest on 12 Mar 2026 by Dan and Zelensky, with framework agreements on energy cooperation and a joint statement on producing Ukrainian defence systems, including drones, in Romania; it follows the 1997 Basic Political Treaty.

sources.title: Romania, Ukraine sign strategic partnership declaration during Zelensky's visit to Bucharest
Romania signs deal with Ukraine on joint defence production including drones

relations_from.summary: Strategic partnership with Turkiye, described by Dan in June 2026 as a fifteen-year partnership whose scope he proposed to widen to Black Sea undersea infrastructure; Turkish diplomatic material dates the declaration to 2011, Romanian sources to 2015.

sources.title: President Dan says strategic partnership between Romania and Turkey could be expanded

relations_from.summary: About 1,000 US troops remain in Romania after the Pentagon decided (29 Oct 2025) not to replace the 2nd Brigade of the 101st Airborne; both Armed Services chairs opposed the decision. Kyiv Post's sources put the cut at a battalion, not a brigade.

sources.title: Naval Support Facility Deveselu
US Embassy: Aegis Ashore Romania is fully operational

relations_from.summary: Parliament approved the purchase of 32 F-35A fighters for an estimated USD 6.5bn, Romania's most expensive military buy; deliveries are expected in the early 2030s. One database lists 48; the signed-deal reporting says 32.

sources.title: Romania to buy F-35 fighter jets

relations_from.summary: Within a day of the US request, the Supreme Council of National Defence and Parliament approved (11 Mar 2026) use of Mihail Kogalniceanu for refuelling aircraft, surveillance and satellite equipment in the US Iran operation (Epic Fury); Rutte later named Romania and Italy as participants and Iran accused NATO of complicity (June 2026).

relations_from.summary: Romania joined the NATO Hague Summit commitment (June 2025) to a long-term defence ambition of 5% of GDP; actual spending was 2.24-2.45% of GDP in 2025 depending on the source (1.58% in 2023), and the official 2026 outturn was not found.

sources.title: Romania defence spending profile

relations_from.summary: On 8 Jul 2026, at the NATO summit in Ankara, the defence ministers of Romania, Bulgaria and Turkiye signed an amendment to the Black Sea mine-countermeasures task group memorandum adding protection of critical underwater infrastructure; the group, operational since 1 Jul 2024, rotates command every six months (Romania Jul 2025-Jan 2026, Turkiye, then Bulgaria from 9 Jul 2026).

Romania, Bulgaria, Turkiye sign Black Sea mine group amendment at NATO summit

relations_from.summary: Full Schengen entry: the Council decided on 12 Dec 2024 to lift internal land border checks with and between Romania and Bulgaria from 1 Jan 2025, after Austria dropped its veto; air and sea checks had ended on 31 Mar 2024.

Romania, Bulgaria become full members of EU's Schengen zone

relations_from.summary: The Constitutional Court annulled the whole presidential election on 6 Dec 2024, days before the runoff, after President Iohannis declassified intelligence alleging a Russian-run campaign (thousands of accounts on TikTok and Telegram, 25,000 paid accounts, over EUR 1m in donations) for Calin Georgescu. The prosecutor-general called him the 'beneficiary of Russia's hybrid war actions'; he is on trial for complicity in an attempted coup (trial confirmed April 2026). Whether he knew of the campaign is unclear.

sources.title: Constitutional Court nullifies Romania's presidential election
Romania's top court annuls presidential vote won by far-right candidate
Court rules to continue coup d'etat trial of far-right Romanian politician Calin Georgescu, mercenaries

relations_from.summary: Russian drones repeatedly enter Romanian airspace from Ukraine: F-16s scrambled in September 2025; a drone hit a residential building in Galati on 29 May 2026, wounding two; Romanian F-16s shot down their first drone (a Geran-2) near Padina, Buzau, on 24 Jul 2026 and a second on 25 Jul; on 2 Aug a drone crossed near Tulcea and was downed by Ukraine. The 2025 law allows destroying drones as a last resort.

Romania shoots down second drone in two days
Romanian jets scramble as Russian drone enters NATO airspace before Ukraine shoots it down

relations_from.summary: After the Galati strike Romania declared the Russian consul in Constanta persona non grata and withdrew permission for the consulate (29 May 2026); Moscow answered on 25 Jun by expelling Romania's consul general in St Petersburg and closing the consulate there.

sources.title: The Romanian mission will no longer operate in one of Russia's major cities

relations_from.summary: On 27 Jul 2026, after three drones were shot down, Romania summoned the Russian ambassador, showed him debris confirmed by prosecutors as Russian, declared an embassy staff member persona non grata (five days to leave) and recalled its ambassador in Moscow for consultations; Moscow expelled a Romanian embassy employee on 26-27 Aug.

relations_from.summary: Romania applies the US and UK sanctions on Lukoil (October 2025) without seeking an extension of the deadline (November 2025); the Petrotel Ploiesti refinery (about a fifth to a quarter of national fuel output) stayed shut after maintenance, the state sought to run it with a US licence in spring 2026, and it entered insolvency in late August 2026 (single-source). Lukoil also holds 300 petrol stations and a majority of the Trident Black Sea block.

relations_from.summary: Law signed by Iohannis on 11 Jun 2021 lets only suppliers approved by the Prime Minister, after a Supreme Council of National Defence assessment, supply 5G equipment; Huawei's authorisation was refused and Huawei sued in the Bucharest Court of Appeal. It followed the 2019 US-Romania memorandum. In November 2025 Dan said the National Defence Strategy gives China special attention but that Romania should not break relations.

relations_to.summary: Vertical Corridor: the Greece-Bulgaria-Romania-Moldova-Ukraine gas route, with seven transmission operators; capacity extensions at Kulata/Sidirokastro and Negru Voda/Kardam are due by end-2026 (Stara Zagora and Komotini in 2027); a March 2026 tariff revision cut costs, and a July 2026 auction at Sidirokastro booked over 45% of capacity across four gas years.

relations_to.summary: Romania is the gateway for diversified energy: the Iași-Ungheni gas pipeline (43 km, up to 1.5 bcm/year, inaugurated 2020) and 110 kV electricity links; a 400 kV Bălți-Suceava line is planned in the National Development Plan, and import capacity is limited until the high-voltage links are built. Press reports say Romania became the main source of Moldovan electricity imports in 2025 (not verified at source).
